claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a metastable BCC solid solution.
The starting powder has a high defect density and may contain surface oxide layers.
SPS at 950–1000 °C, 30–50 MPa, and 10–15 minutes under vacuum or inert gas is an appropriate processing window for this alloy.
Temperatures below 800 °C provide insufficient atomic mobility for phase separation and grain-boundary wetting.
Keeping the temperature below 1000 °C prevents excessive magnesium vaporization.
An oxygen-free atmosphere prevents uncontrolled surface oxidation during the critical diffusion period.
Sintering at 950–1000 °C causes rapid Mg and Al diffusion.
Rapid diffusion produces a continuous nanoscale network of Al-Fe-rich intermetallic precipitates at BCC grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary intermetallic may have a B2 or Laves structure.
Negative Al-Fe mixing enthalpy locally overcomes the configurational-entropy stabilization of the BCC phase.
The Al-Fe-rich phase forms by spinodal decomposition or grain-boundary nucleation.
The percolating intermetallic network blocks Mg diffusion paths and thereby suppresses Mg volatilization and density loss.
The intermetallic network blocks oxygen transport and thereby improves oxidation or corrosion resistance.
Interfaces between the intermetallic precipitates and the BCC matrix impede dislocation motion and increase hardness.
Lattice distortion in the retained BCC solid solution contributes to increased hardness.
The proposed processing window will produce a dual-phase bulk alloy with greater than 98% theoretical density.
The resulting alloy will have Vickers hardness greater than 400 HV.
The resulting passive film will have lower ionic conductivity than films on specimens sintered below 800 °C or above 1000 °C.
Sintering below 800 °C produces porous, low-hardness material that remains single-phase BCC.
Sintering above 1000 °C causes Mg loss, compositional deviation, porosity, and coarse discontinuous intermetallics with poor mechanical and corrosion properties.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and intervention include 1000 °C in the operative range, whereas the conditions require the temperature to be strictly below 1000 °C.
